points: This chapter is after Yoshiyahu's death, under Yehoyakim, about 20 years before the churban. The first pesukim demand that we be authentic, not two-faced.
"Plow properly, don't sow among thorns": the Malbim says the thorns are bad middos. Work on being a kind, good person first, and then spiritual growth can take root.
Yirmiyahu seems to say, "Hashem, You misled this people." The Abarbanel: they took Yonah's story to mean Hashem forgives no matter what. But Ninveh was forgiven because they did teshuvah.

Yoshiyahu refused to let Egypt pass through the land, sure that a righteous nation needs no war, and was killed. Chazal say the people hid idols behind their doors. Overconfidence is a mistake we still make.
"Tohu vavohu": the people felt Judaism was over, like after the Holocaust. Hashem promises devastation, but not complete destruction; there will be a future.
